title: What the Kea gets into

is_this_you.pressure: Pressure makes you funnier. You crack the joke first and fix the latch second, and by then half the hut is helping.
is_this_you.love: You court with questions and keep poking until the other person pokes back. The ones who laugh get to stay.
is_this_you.cost: Some days you take the blame for a mess you only flew over to look at.

opener.text: Say the bird's name out loud and you are doing its call. Kea copies the sound it makes, keee aaa [s1] [s3]. The Waitaha people held it among their kaitiaki, the guardians of the people, beside the harrier and the morepork [s1]. Loud, nosy, and on the guard roster. That is you.

howto: Three parts. Poke at them in any order.

tabs.label: Curiosity
tabs.intro: Air that asks. Metal that handles.

rows.text: Gemini is mutable Air, ruled by Mercury, the planet of quick talk and new information [s7] [s8]. The Monkey is yang Metal, read as witty, mischievous and a fast learner [s9] [s10]. Put the two together and every question heads straight for your hands. You understand a thing best once it is in pieces on the table, and you narrate the teardown while you do it.

The kea is the world's only mountain parrot, at home in New Zealand's Southern Alps [s3]. It investigates with its beak, its tongue and its claws [s2]. Car accessories and ski lodge gear come apart under that attention; researchers call it opportunistic exploration [s4]. Hut stories add stolen nails, hidden away sorted by size [s2]. Someone always has to check how the thing works. You volunteer.

tabs.label: Your flock
tabs.intro: Three birds for your flock, and one to give room.
tabs.love_lead: In love your laugh does the courting. Researchers played wild kea a recording of the play call, and the birds that heard it played more and for longer [s5]. The old Chinese pairings put three of them in your flock.

rows.text: Pick work where taking things apart is the job. Testing, repair and security research all pay someone to find the weak latch before anyone else does.

Young kea travel together in flocks for two or three years before they settle [s4]. Their pecking order is not necessarily a straight line [s4]. You do best in a loose crew where the youngest can still win a round.

easy.why: The Red Panda (Libra, Rat year) shares your trine of Rat, Dragon and Monkey, and Libra is Air like you [s11] [s7].
The Mantis Shrimp (Aquarius, Dragon year) closes the same trine, and Aquarius brings more Air to keep the talk going [s11].
The Paradise Tanager (Libra, Snake year) is your secret friend, since Snake and Monkey make one of the six harmonies pairs [s11].

hard.why: The hard one is the Lanner Falcon: the Tiger clashes with the Monkey, and Sagittarius sits opposite Gemini [s11] [s7].

story.text: When sheep farming reached the high country in the 1870s, farmers blamed the kea, a bounty followed, and an estimated 150,000 birds were shot before full protection came in 1986 [s2]. In 2017 New Zealand voted it Bird of the Year, with 7,311 votes [s6]. Same bird. Same cheek.

closing: Keep poking. Sort the nails by size afterward, so they know it was you.
